And he swore to him
that when he fought against the Persians,
he would also release his father from exile (imprisonment?).
And when it was said to him that he should participate with the Synodites, that is to say, the Chalcedonians,
he made an excuse and said
that all the tribes of the Arabs are of the Diacrinomenoi, that is, the Orthodox,
and if I convert, they will kill me.
And when Na'man departed, he swore
that he would never again see the face of the Romans by his own will.
Now the Romans heard this,
and while he was on the road, they seized him and exiled him as well.
And the kingdom of the Arabs was divided into fifteen chiefs.
And most of them joined the Persians,
and some of them joined the Chalcedonians.
And others cast off their weapons and dwelt in cities and villages in the land of Sinjar, in Assyria, and in Syria;
and unto this day they have been preserved in Orthodoxy,
such as those in Haditha, Hit, Beth Arabaye, Qaryatayn which is in the region of Homs, Nabk, and the rest of the places.
At this time, a certain Persian sorcerer said
that he was the eldest son of King Khosrow;
the one who, when his forces chose his blind son Hormizd to reign over them,
his father took pity on him and gave him provisions and sent him away so that he would not be killed.
This man came to the Roman forces that were in Armenia and said
that he would surrender the kingdom of the Persians to the Romans,
provided that the king of the Romans gave him an army.
And the Romans informed Tiberius,
and he rejoiced greatly over him.
And he sent gold and royal garments,
and ordered that he should come with great pomp to the imperial city.
And when he arrived at Chalcedon,
the king sent his spatharios (the sword-bearer?) of the king of the Persians,
to investigate whether it was him or not.
And when he saw him and recognized him,
he seized him by his hair and threw him from the throne, and said:
"You impostor, do you sit upon a throne
while nobles stand before you?" Now that miserable man, when he feared death,
became a Christian.
At this time, while the Roman army had marched against Persia with Maurice Caesar,
the barbarian peoples of the Avars, the Slavs, and the Lombards, who were in subjugation to the Khagan,
were devastating the territories of the Romans.
And also Adharman the marzban reached Edessa,
and cast fire into it,
and burned thirty-eight churches and monasteries.
